text:
paul: Noticing a steady increase in tiny-gpu Pending in us-west2 for ~75m. ~330 pods Pending, nodes show fractional slots free but scheduling fails due to strict topology affinity :frowning:
nina: Which affinity? nvlink/socket? namespace?
paul: nodeAffinity required: topology.kubernetes.io/socket=local. New racks report socket=hybrid on half of nodes. 
omar: Pod describe shows: 0/192 nodes are available: 96 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/selector, 96 node(s) had taint {gpu:reserved=true:NoSchedule}.
claire: Inventory sync failed during last rollout, labels defaulted -> label drift.
paul: Quick options: (A) run inventory relabel (evictions risk) (B) deploy mutating webhook to relax required->preferred for annotated tiny pods (C) mark certain nodes socket=partial and add scheduler weight fallback.
nina: Ops preference is C + brief webhook in canary. We want minimal pod mutation.
omar: Also watch conntrack; last time a mass bind pushed it above 85%. devops-bot: conntrack us-west2: 71% (warn 80%).
claire: Plan: 1) dry-run label script on pool mixed-racks 2) if dry-run good, label as socket=partial 3) deploy webhook to namespace tiny-gpu-canary only to relax affinity for annotated pods 4) monitor Pending, conntrack, scheduling latency 5) roll forward/rollback in 10m windows.
paul: I'll own monitoring and alerts. Nina do the dry run and post results.
nina: Running `./tools/label-sync --dry-run --pool=mixed-racks` now. Posting output in 5m.
claire: Postmortem follow-ups: fix inventory sync, add admission guard to prevent unlabeled nodes, and add a scheduler test for mixed-label clusters.
paul: Thanks team. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
